//: Editor configuration ONLY. It has no effect on the deployed worker:
Cloudflare builds it with esbuild via wrangler, and node runs the tests.
Neither reads this file.
It exists so the editor resolves the project's own ESM the way the tools
that actually load it do. The repository's .mjs test files import each
other with full relative paths, and without a jsconfig the language
server defaults to moduleResolution 'node10', which does not resolve the
'.js' extension on a relative ESM import - so it reports modules that
exist, and that node loads on the very next line, as missing.
It also documents the one hard deployment constraint, which is easy to
violate by accident:
For Cloudflare/worker.js is pasted into the Cloudflare dashboard, and
the dashboard has no filesystem. The worker therefore MUST NOT import
anything, from anywhere, ever. An import is invisible to node, to
wrangler, and to all 23 security gates - it only fails as a paste, at
deploy time, by hand.
tools/single_file_worker_test.mjs enforces that, and its S1/S2 failure
message says so.
'bundler' rather than 'nodenext': it matches how these files are actually
consumed (a bundler plus node's ESM loader), and it does not impose
Node's stricter ESM rules on files that are never published as packages.
